plan.english: What carries the burden of the wagon? The wheel transports it.
What is stretched and slays the horned one? It is the bow.
What carries the people about? It is the team.
Who swims on the sea and goes to the nest? It is the duck.
Who is alert and guards the nest? It is the goose.
Who saw the ram from the sky and was gripping it? It was the eagle.
Who strikes with the hoof and carries a man? It is the stallion.
What did the goose make? She made a nest.
What burns, which comes from the oak? It is resin.
What covers the hazel and is not a garment? It is hoarfrost.
What clothes the hazel? It is darkness.
What is red and goes out of the wound? It is blood.
What is sharp and is not bronze? It is the tooth.
What is sweet and kills a man? It is poison.
What goes, and no ruler makes it stand? It is the year.
What appears from the sea and gives brightness? It is the day.
Whom did the sky split? It is the oak.
What joins two wild bulls? It is the yoke.
Who ploughs and is not a man? It is the yoked stallion.
What went from me, and you do not see it? It is a word.
What carries the burden and swallows the dead? It is the sea.
What is sweet, and you drink it? It is juice.
What is dead and kills the wild bull? It is the spear.
What goes on wheels, and a stallion drives it? It is the wagon.
Who lies and does not see the day? The man is dead.
Who wears a garment, and I did not make it? It is the ram.
What eats the oak and is afraid of the liquid? It is the burning.
What is sharp and stirs the tears? It is garlic.
Who stands, and no ruler has reached him? It is the sky.
What does the man give the mistress, and she wears it? It is a ring.
Whoever kills the other shall give the payment.
Let the lord protect the people.
Whoever strikes the other, let him give the payment for the wound.
Whoever seizes the garment of one of the two shall give a ram and bronze.
Whoever leads the mistress shall give the bride price to the master.
Do not move the boundary! It belongs to the ruler.
Whoever gives poison to a ruler, let him die.
Let the word be faithful.
Whoever breaks the word shall die.
Let the master place the yoke.
Whoever leaves the dowry at the crossing shall give bronze.
Whoever kills a warrior in the war shall not give the payment.
Whoever burns the hazel shall give a garment.
Whoever splits the tooth of the lord shall give a ram.
Let the master guard the burden.
Do not split the oak with bronze!
Do not kill the horned one in the seventh year!
Let the measure be faithful.
Let him give a full measure.
On the seventh day let the people sit down.
Let the ruler clothe the naked.
Let the old man speak the word.
Do not lead the man out in the darkness!
Whoever is thirsty, let him drink.
Let the one carry the burden and let the other drive the stallion.
Let the daughter-in-law listen to the mistress.
Let the brother-in-law guard the daughter-in-law.
Let the one divide the plunder.
Do not kill the eagle!
Whoever leaves the brother-in-law shall die.
Who are you, and what do you seek?
I am a warrior, and I seek the lord.
What did you see? I have seen a wild bull.
Listen, brother-in-law! A wild bull is coming.
Do not tremble!
Stand up and seize the spear!
Let us go to the sea.
Give me the bow, and I will give you a ring.
May the sky protect you!
May you live, daughter-in-law!
I know the horned one, and I do not know the word.
What did you come to know? I know the boundary.
Is the spear sharp? It is sharp.
Who killed the horned one? I struck it.
I came from the crossing. I am thirsty. Give me the juice!
Sit down by the hazel and drink the juice!
The garlic is boiling. Cook the goose!
Eat the duck and be satisfied!
Are you satisfied? I am satisfied.
The sore is swelling. Smear it with resin!
Make the spear straight, warrior!
Heat the bronze, and I shall be at work.
The warrior is sweating. Let him sip.
Dry the garment!
Renew the old yoke!
Do not swim in the sea!
Let us settle by the oak.
May the goose be productive!
The year makes the lord old.
I am born of the sky.
The duck is full-grown.
Be alert! The day is appearing.
Stay awake, daughter-in-law!
I trust the brother-in-law.
Remember my word.
Who has power? I have power.
The mistress hears well.
Look at the nest! The eagle is gone.
I want to see the eagle.
Show me the horned one!
Point out the crossing to the people.
Follow me! I am leading.
Creep to the nest, and do not walk!
Track the wild bull by the hoof!
Hide the ring! Do not show it!
The master sits, and the daughter-in-law stands.
Seat the old man!
Who milks the sheep? The mistress milks.
The master ploughs, and the brother-in-law milks.
What are you arranging? I am arranging the burden.
The wheel is breaking! Stop the wagon!
Stretch the bow!
The old man holds up the burden.
Do not break the bow!
Split the hazel!
Is the ruler alive? He is alive.
Is he dead? He is not dead. He breathes.
Do you hear the eagle? I hear it.
I see the geese. They are black.
The wagon is full, and the wheel is light.
May the lord be praised!
The juice is libated. Drink it!
Let us sit down and eat.
Come, brother-in-law! We shall drive the wagon.
Who leads the people? The lord leads.
Say the request! I am listening.
Have you seen the swelling?
Take a step to the top!
Trust the ordinance!
Dress yourself! It is getting dark.
I am the praised one, and I know the fight.
I slew the first, and I slew the other.
The first struck the black one, and he died.
He struck him in the liver, and he died.
The hip was pierced with the spear.
He thrust the sharp one into the hip.
He cut off the top of the oak.
He knew the taste of blood.
Strength and might were in him.
War stirred the people, and they were afraid.
The old man spoke, and the praised one listened.
The praised one became old.
He trembled at the fight, and he did not leave.
The warrior overcame the black one.
He split the hip with a spear.
The first struck, and he trembled.
Now the fight came about, and they trembled.
He stood steady in the fight, and he struck.
The black one slew the first, and the praised one slew him.
The sea swallowed the boundary.
They divided the plunder.
He left the plunder and went.
Strength was leaving him.
Might stood in him.
The wound swelled, and he smeared it with resin.
Blood went from the wound.
Poison was in the sharp one.
The shine of the bronze was red.
The darkness covered the fight.
He broke the tooth, and the blood was red.
The yoked ones transported the wagon, and it was full.
He drove to the crossing, and the wheel broke.
He joined the stallions with the yoke, and he went.
The praised one stood up, and he was alert.
It was getting dark, and he stopped the yoked ones.
The wild bull licked the blood, and it sweated.
They arrived at the hazel, and they settled.
He put on a garment, and he went.
Tears appeared from the master.
They laid the dead one down, and they bowed.
He made a request, and they heard it.
He established the ordinance, and they listened.
He gave the bride price and led the mistress.
The year made the alert one old.
The days were sweet.
The hoarfrost lay on the bottom.

He gave the stallion a measure of juice.
The burning ate the nest.

He gave the nourishment to the black one, and it was full.
The breadth of the crossing was black.
He joined the harrow with the yoke, and he ploughed.
The bottom of the wound was red.
The befoulement lay on the top.
He listened to the request, and he bowed.
The ordinance was faithful, and he knew it.
Now the war came to the boundary, and he was alert.
He was awake in the darkness, and he did not tremble.
Tears came from him, and he sat down.
The tears were dried.
He saw the tears of the daughter-in-law.
Strength grew in him.
Strength rose in him, and he stood up.
Might overcame the fight.
Might was with the alert one.
The troops arrived at the boundary.
The troops settled at the crossing, and they were thirsty.
They carried the plunder and sat down.
He lifted the plunder, and it lay in the darkness.

He seized the payment, and it was full.
He sipped the liquid, and he came to know the taste.
He cooked the garlic, and the taste was sweet.

The taste of the resin was sharp.
The burning was red.
The burning stood on the top.
The shine of the day was lightweight.
Shine appeared from the sky.
One of the two struck, and the other trembled.
One of the two went, and he left.
One of the two was alert, and he was awake.
The eagle sat on the top, and it saw the duck.
He stood on the top and looked at the plunder.
The liver was red.

The hoof was sharp.
The hoof struck the liver.
The measure was full.
In the seventh year he arrived.
The naked one trembled, and the sheltered one stood steady.
The drunk one lay down, and the light one crept.
He was naked, and he was afraid.
He was light, and he walked in the darkness.
He was drunk, and he sat down.
He was sheltered, and he was awake.

The faithful ordinance stood.
The yoked ones stood steady.
He took the seventh payment.
The sharp hoof split the liver.

He placed the ring on the bottom.
He was making the ring.
He was making the bow, and the bow was stretched.
He was straightening the harrow.
The swelling was dried.
The seventh year was productive.
He smeared the harrow with resin.
He recognized the duck by the taste.
The goose followed him.
The horned one leaned, and the sheep drank.
He said the request.
He was saying the ordinance, and they listened.
The warrior breathed, and he died.
